title: Spatial Showroom
description: UI design and UX research for the Omnia Virtual Showroom, a Vision Pro car showroom built for a Tesla event in four months and now live on the visionOS App Store.
hmw: showcase a virtual car showroom and allow for full, realistic customization to potential business and consumer customers?

blocks.text: A Tesla showroom event needed an XR demo that was easy enough to run for about 100 people. Over four months at Omnia, I was UI designer and UX researcher on the app.
The Omnia Virtual Showroom is live on the visionOS App Store.
Twenty-five interviews and a configurator review

I conducted 25+ interviews with traditional media users, creators looking to publish spatial content, headset owners and company founders, who spoke to business use cases. I evaluated name-brand web car configurators, which put functionality and configuration options ahead of AR features, and took their functional ideas into a Vision Pro app with more features. I organized a full-stack team around development, backend and 3D model delivery, and prototyped in Figma and then in code. With the team, I turned the findings into personas for tech-savvy buyers and for people who need to see a car in real life, and into affinity maps of pain points and prioritized features.

Tesla of River North approached our company to create an XR app for their showroom event on November 21st, 2024. After a few discussions, we settled on a virtual car showroom with customization options and fun, quirky features to draw people in. Using our strengths in visionOS and mobile XR development, we got to work. Paper sketches became FigJam mockups of the landing page and the car-viewing UI. Users go through a step to place their car, which also lets the app load the heavy 3D model in the background.

A Tesla showroom in your own home. You can view the products life-size and interact with them as if you owned them, and customize the colors, wheel designs and interior features before placing an order.

The Tesla showroom event aimed to draw potential buyers and people curious about futuristic tech. Visitors needed to see Tesla’s cars and their appeal, along with new tech that would leave them in awe. The app had to be easy to demo to about 100 people, a few minutes each, as a quick plug-and-play setup with minimal setup time.
Two calls that shaped the showroom

cards.label: Place-your-car step
cards.value: The team chose a place-your-car step before the viewer, because it let the app load the heavy 3D model in the background.

cards.label: Configurator depth
cards.value: Chose to borrow the configuration depth of web car configurators, which put functionality ahead of AR features, and extend it on Vision Pro.

items: The proof is that the app is live on the App Store and was built for the event. I have no recorded results from the event itself.
“Demo to about 100 people” was the requirement the design had to meet, not a result I measured.
